body:
ORDERING GUARANTEE THAT APPLIES: GLOBAL — one durable commit-observation position shared by all readers of the store. Record A (`docs/engineering/09-ordering-contract-a.md`) is the applicable statement; Record B (`09-ordering-contract-b.md`) is contradicted by the pinned contract this workspace actually consumes.

WHAT THE WORKSPACE IS
This is the Palimpsest plugin (`package.json` name `palimpsest-dsh`) whose cross-repo integration is with Ordarium. Its subscribed artifacts are pinned at Ordarium v1.3.1 (`package.json:32-34`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-18`): `@ordarium/core` 1.3.1 (installed), `@ordarium/ledger-sqlite` 1.3.1, `@ordarium/host-kit` 1.3.1, plus `@ordarium/testing` 1.3.1. Per `docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md` §0, the authority order is explicit: Ordarium contract truth lives in Ordarium's own contract/artifacts; Palimpsest-side records only restate it. So the subscribed artifact is the deciding source, not the prose records.

DECIDING EVIDENCE (pinned 1.3.1)
- Contract surface: `@ordarium/core` `StateChangePage.cursor` is documented verbatim as "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change", and the feed is "committed state revisions in durable ledger commit-observation order, ascending (ORD-BOOT-0)"; `cursor` is always present so a consumer reaching the end still holds a durable resume position (`node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/types.d.ts`). `StateChangeFilter` (namespace/limit) only narrows which changes are delivered.
- Storage: one sequence per store — `ordarium_state_changes(change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, ...)`, written in the same transaction as the revision, so a committed revision and its observable position are never split (`@ordarium/ledger-sqlite/dist/src/index.js` compareAndSetState; `migrations.js` createStateTables).
- Read path: `changes()` does `ORDER BY c.change_seq ASC` and validates the caller cursor against `#stateChangeHighWater()` — the whole-ledger high-water mark, with the explicit comment that "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position … this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence. Concurrent commits only raise the mark, so a valid cursor cannot be falsely rejected; a restored/replaced ledger lowers it and fails closed" (`InvalidCursorError`).
- The volatile `MemoryLedger` mirrors it: a single `#stateChanges` array, contiguous positions 1..n, validated against its own length (`@ordarium/core/dist/src/ledger.js`).

CONSEQUENCE
All consumers observe one total commit order across all namespaces; a filter returns a subsequence of that one order; the same numeric position denotes the same ledger commit for every consumer. Monotonicity is guaranteed (commits only raise the mark); cursor tampering/loss fails closed rather than silently restarting. One bounded honesty caveat: the v3→v4 migration backfills synthetic positions in (namespace, key, revision) order, explicitly labelled migration order rather than original commit order; from v4 on, new commits carry the real durable database order.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY PER-CONSUMER
Only the opaque cursor token is consumer-held: each consumer stores its own resume point and may sit at a different position. That is client-local state over the single global order — not a per-consumer ordering as Record B asserts. "per-consumer" occurs nowhere else in the repository, while Record A's wording ("filter-independent", "one position shared") matches the shipped contract. The superficially similar per-consumer cursor in this repo (`viewCursor`, PLMP-PARSE-1 / docs/engineering/35) governs Palimpsest's own graph-view freshness and is a different, explicitly-separated concept from the Ordarium state-change feed.

DECISION ON PEER CONTACT
Both records claim "normative, current scope" and directly contradict each other, but the conflict is between two Palimpsest-side restatements of an Ordarium contract face, so local provenance decides it: version scope (the current pinned line is 1.3.1/schema v4, which introduced the ORD-BOOT-0 feed) plus the §0 authority order plus the subscribed artifact. No load-bearing source remains unresolved and nothing peer-owned is missing, so no peer contact is warranted. Incidental version lag is noted but immaterial: the engineering docs and `test/ordarium_ledger.test.ts` still speak of 1.2.0/schema v3 while the pinned artifacts are 1.3.1/schema v4.
